mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.0% signals a tightening monetary policy regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals tight labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 3.5%, or the mean return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits above 1.45 million units signals strong housing demand and rising consumer confidence, which forecasts higher future consumption and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1450.0, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 102.0 index points signals weakening manufacturing activity and deteriorating business conditions, which reduces corporate profitability expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 102.0, or the mean return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in both personal consumption expenditures (PAYEMS) and residential construction (HOUST) signals broad-based demand strength, which increases corporate revenue visibility and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and HOUST fails to produce positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in interaction regression).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in CPI inflation above 3.5% combined with a stable federal funds rate signals persistent inflationary pressure, prompting market expectations of prolonged restrictive policy, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5 and FEDFUNDS is stable, or the interaction term in a regression model is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment and a decline in the unemployment rate signals a robust labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to generate positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 700,000 million dollars, combined with a positive GDP growth rate (GDPC1 > 0.5% q/q), signals strong aggregate demand momentum that supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising RSAFS and positive GDPC1 fails to produce positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a predictive model is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
